name: US Sonic Dollar
oneLiner: USSD is Sonic Labs's permissionless 1:1 dollar built on Frax's frxUSD infrastructure, backed by tokenized U.S. Treasury products and approved stablecoins.
collateral: Short-duration tokenized U.S. Treasury products held by approved custodians: BlackRock BUIDL (USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund), Superstate USTB (Short Duration U.S. Government Securities Fund), and WisdomTree WTGXX (Government Money Market Digital Fund); supported minting collateral also includes USDC, USDT, PYUSD, and USDB
pegMechanism: 1:1 permissionless mint and redemption via non-custodial smart contracts built on Frax's frxUSD infrastructure; users mint with any approved USD asset (USDC, USDT, PYUSD, USDB, BUIDL, USTB, WTGXX) at zero fee; redeem into any supported USD asset at any time with no lockup or withdrawal delay; cross-chain via CCTP; yield from Treasury reserves flows to the Sonic ecosystem rather than to USSD holders

applicabilityBasis.summary: Sonic Labs markets USSD as a Treasury-backed, 1:1 mint/redeem dollar built on GENIUS-compatible frxUSD infrastructure; the issuer's public positioning treats it as a payment stablecoin subject to the GENIUS Act.

genius.notes: Sonic Labs publicly markets USSD as 'fully compatible with the GENIUS Act' and has established Sonic USA LLC (Delaware) for U.S. regulatory engagement. No PPSI application, OCC/FDIC/Federal Reserve filing, or state-qualified authorization has been found. The GENIUS Act rulemaking remains in proposed-rules phase with no PPSI approvals granted to any issuer as of 2026-06-18. Foreign exception status updated to not-applicable as the issuer is U.S.-domiciled.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No token-specific PPSI approval, state-qualified approval, official GENIUS Act application filing, or comparable foreign-issuer exception was located for USSD or Sonic Labs / Sonic USA LLC in any federal or state regulatory database. Sonic Labs' GENIUS compatibility claims are issuer marketing, not regulatory disclosures.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Explicit Yes retained: centralized governance metadata indicates issuer or admin control; registry links were reviewed for direct freeze, blacklist, pause, burn, or upgrade authority.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USSD uses Frax/LayerZero OFT-style omnichain infrastructure for cross-chain USSD minting, while CCTP v2 remains a secondary USDC redemption rail. The durable cross-chain risk is therefore the external LayerZero route plus scoped CCTP redemption exposure, not issuer-native CCTP alone.

mintAuthority.summary: USSD is a Sonic Labs dollar built on Frax's frxUSD infrastructure: users mint/redeem 1:1 and non-custodially against an issuer-administered set of approved USD assets, while the issuer/Frax framework custodies tokenized U.S. Treasury reserves (BUIDL/USTB/WTGXX) and manages reserve deployment.

controls.label: frxUSD-based USSD mint/redeem contract
controls.capDescription: Permissionless 1:1 mint against an issuer-administered approved-collateral set (USDC, USDT, PYUSD, USDB, BUIDL, USTB, WTGXX); the approved-asset list and parameters are controlled by the issuer/Frax framework.
controls.evidence: Sonic Labs docs state USSD is built on Frax's frxUSD infrastructure with non-custodial 1:1 mint/redeem and zero fees; the set of approved minting collateral is defined by the issuer.

controls.label: Sonic Labs / Frax reserve custodian + treasury management
controls.evidence: Reserves are custodied tokenized U.S. Treasury products (BlackRock BUIDL, Superstate USTB, WisdomTree WTGXX) with deployment/management run through Frax's infrastructure; yield is directed to the Sonic ecosystem, indicating issuer/custodian control over reserves and the approved-asset roster.

review.evidence: USSD's mint/redeem is permissionless 1:1 against approved USD assets via Frax frxUSD smart contracts, but the approved-collateral set, RWA reserve custody (BUIDL/USTB/WTGXX), and reserve deployment are administered by Sonic Labs / the Frax framework. This is an AMO/custodian-hybrid rather than a pure user-collateralized or pure fiat-issuer model.
review.sourceFreeRationale: frxUSD-based mechanism and reserve composition confirmed from Sonic/Frax materials; the on-chain owner/admin of the USSD contract and the controller of the approved-collateral roster were not independently resolved.
unresolvedQuestions: Resolve the on-chain admin/owner of 0x000000000eccff26b795f73fb0a70d48da657fef and who can modify the approved-collateral set (Sonic Labs multisig vs Frax governance) before raising confidence.
